money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Mauritanian Ouguiya (MRU). It's illegal to import or export ouguiyas. You must declare any foreign currency on arrival, but there are no limits on how much you can import. When you leave Mauritania, you can't have more foreign currency with you than the amount you declared on arrival. Credit cards aren't widely used. Traveller's cheques aren't accepted. Most places only accept cash. Some banks in Nouakchott have ATMs which accept foreign credit cards. Check ATM locations with your bank before you travel. visa-preparation.entry_summary: An electronic visa must be obtained before travelling, from the Mauritanian Ministry of the Interior and Decentralization (ANRPTS portal). Visas are no longer issued on arrival. A yellow fever certificate is required.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Electronic visa online before travel, in 30-day, 90-day or 360-day packages, valid at all international entry points.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Apply on the ANRPTS e-visa portal and wait for authorisation before travelling; carry a yellow fever certificate.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: The e-visa packages are 30, 90 or 360 days.

steps.step: Apply for the e-visa on the ANRPTS portal: choose the duration package, then passport, traveller and trip details.
Wait for authorisation before travelling: there's no visa on arrival.
Carry a yellow fever vaccination certificate.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Islam is the state religion: unauthorised non-Islamic gatherings and proselytising are illegal, and blasphemy carries a maximum penalty of death. Alcohol and pork are banned for everyone; bags are scanned on arrival. During Ramadan do not eat, drink, smoke or chew gum in public in daytime. Dress modestly off the beach (women cover shoulders, no short skirts; men no sleeveless tops or shorts). Ask before photographing people; never photograph security sites. Same-sex activity between men can carry the death penalty. Carry ID copies, especially outside Nouakchott.
